data.gender_notes: Niswa is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Niswa refers to a female companion, friend or wife. It is a term used in the Quran to describe the companions of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The name Niswa carries the meaning “Female companion” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Niswa usually hope their child will grow to embody female companion and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Niswa belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Female companion.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Niswa total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_urdu.name: نسوہ

in_english.name: Niswa
in_english.meaning: A group of women or a feminine community
in_english.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'n-s-ā' which pertains to women, Niswa signifies a gathering or group of women. It appears in the Quran (Surah Al Imran, Verse 143) and holds cultural and spiritual importance in Islamic tradition, symbolizing unity and collective identity among women

It serves as a reminder of the importance of supporting one another in times of need and working together towards common goals. Additionally, the name resonates with the rich heritage of the Prophet Muhammad's companions who played a pivotal role in the spread of Islam and the establishment of Islamic civilization.

The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) taught his followers that true friendship is with Allah alone. By embracing His love and companionship, one can find inner peace, guidance, and support in all aspects of life. The name Niswa can serve as a reminder to always prioritize our relationship with Allah and strive to be His faithful companions. It also emphasizes the importance of building meaningful relationships with others, treating them with kindness, respect, and compassion, just as Allah does for us.
